shortDescription: Stacks up to 7 playable z-levels (3 up / 3 down) into ONE banded RimWorld Map joined by synthetic RegionLink wormholes, so hauling, needs, work and storage come free from vanilla. Cross-level combat, senses, NPC travel, CE bridge (experimental), "Traveler" climb animations, blueprint art, wall risers, research-gated links, a per-colony off switch, Perspective Shift + Toggleable Overlays support. Window 13 inverts click-through to a GLOBAL opt-out at UI.MouseCell/MouseMapPosition (dev tools, psycasts, jumps, mortars and foreign mods all see through air for free), fixes PS's "return to character", and opens CE manned-turret compat.

**⚠ USER WORKING RULES:** (1) NEVER source design ideas from other mods unless asked - scans COMPAT ONLY. **V1 is OUR OWN prior work and is exempt.** (2) Building art = USER via Nano Banana kits. (3) About.xml description = USER's copy. (4) N mockups = N CHOICES.

**What this mod is.** Up to seven z-levels in ONE RimWorld `Map`, banded along +z. Priorities: visual clarity from above, performance, vanilla parity.

**⚠⚠ THE SEVENTY RULES:** 1. CLAMP AT SELECTION. 2. NEVER PATCH `TryRebuildDirtyRegionsAndRooms`. 3. REGION CONNECTIVITY IS MORE OPTIMISTIC THAN THE PATHFINDER: flood CELLS. 4. COUNT EMITTERS/POPULATIONS/ENGINE STACKS. 5 (§48): A `Touch` TARGET IS USUALLY UNWALKABLE. 6 (§49): A VANILLA HELPER CAN BE A NO-OP INSTEAD OF AN ERROR. 7 (§52): THE CARVE IS NOT THE LAST WORD. 8 (§52.6): A LOAD-TIME REPAIR PASS MUST NEVER RE-CREATE WHAT THE PLAYER DELIBERATELY REMOVED. 9 (§53): SOME MISPLACEMENTS ARE NOT VISIBLE IN THE CELL. 10 (§54): A STRUCTURE IS NOT A CELL. 11 (§55): A CELL-LEVEL VERDICT CANNOT AUTHORIZE A PAWN-LEVEL ACTION. 12 (§56a): A FOREIGN MOD'S MAP-SIZE SNAPSHOT IS AN INPUT YOU CAN CORRECT. 13 (§56g): NEVER COPY A GRID YOU DID NOT WATCH BEING WRITTEN. 14 (§56m): BEFORE RELOCATING DATA, ASK WHAT IS ALREADY AT THE DESTINATION. 15 (§57i): ASSERT ALWAYS, NARRATE ON REQUEST. 16 (§56o): COUNT THE FOREIGN MOD'S WRITE PATHS. 17 (§56q): A PASSING RUN THAT DID NOT REPRODUCE THE FAILURE IS NOT A FIX. 18 (§57a): **NEVER EXONERATE A SUSPECT ON ONE CLEAN SAMPLE** - grep version at rule 54. 19 (§57f): `TicksGame` RESTARTS AT 0 EVERY NEW GAME. 20 (§57g): MOVING WORK EARLIER TURNS ON EVERY "IS THIS MAP READY" GATE. 21 (§58): THE PARALLEL GRIDS DO NOT TRAVEL WITH THE CONTENT. 22 (§59): A DERIVED GRID HAS NO PAWN IN IT. 23 (§60): AUDIT THE WEIGHTING, NOT THE SYMBOL. 24 (§61a): CLAMPING A VALUE WITHOUT CLAMPING ITS TARGET BUILDS AN OSCILLATOR. 25 (§61b): A POSTFIX ON `Update` IS AFTER THE OBJECT WAS ALREADY POSITIONED. 26 (§61f): EVERY READ OF THE MAP THE PLAYER CAN REACH MUST PASS THE RENDERER'S "IS IT DRAWN" GATE - selectable is drawable, and so is **highlightable** (§83). 27 (§62c): PREFER SPAWN/DESPAWN OVER FLICK. 28 (§63a): A PERMANENT FICTION INSTALLED FOR ONE SUBSYSTEM IS READ AS FACT BY EVERY OTHER ONE. 29 (§0b): REPORT OUTCOMES, NOT INTENTIONS. 30 (§66d): A FELT DURATION IS A CHAIN, NOT A NUMBER. 31 (§66f): MAKE THE GUARD SAY WHICH CLAUSE DECLINED. 32 (§69a): TURNING OFF A TICK TURNS OFF EVERY SERVICE THAT RODE ON IT. 33 (§62k): A FILTER THAT CAN REJECT EVERYTHING MUST SAY SO. 34 (§62l): AN INVISIBLE THING IS ABSENT FROM EVERY SECTION LAYER. 35 (§62n): A CLONED FOREIGN DEF MADE VISIBLE IS IN NONE OF THE HOST'S OWN LOOKUPS. 36 (§70a): RUN VANILLA'S OWN LEGALITY PREDICATE. 37 (§71a): NAME THE ENFORCEMENT POINT BEFORE NAMING THE SYMPTOM. 38 (§73): WHEN A SPRITE MUST APPEAR AWAY FROM ITS THING'S POSITION, OWN THE DRAW - **and §84.8's other half: when a thing insists on drawing itself at a position of its OWN, the offset must be applied to THAT position, not to the one you pass it.** 39 (§76): WINNING THE LAST WRITE DOES NOT SETTLE A DISAGREEMENT ABOUT THE TARGET. 40 (§75.h): A TRIPWIRE THAT FIRES BEFORE THE OBSERVER ATTACHES IS NOT A TRIPWIRE. 41 (§77a): A STRUCT FIELD YOU NEVER SET IS A FEATURE YOU NEVER SHIPPED. 42 (§77b): THE DIRECTION A MOTION READS AS IS A PROPERTY OF THE THING, NOT OF THE ARRIVAL. 43 (§78): **DEFER THE MOVE, NEVER THE DECISION.** 44 (§78b): AN OFFSET APPLIED WHOLE ON FRAME ONE IS A TELEPORT. 45 (§78d): **A DIRECTION OF TRAVEL IS NOT A DIRECTION OF ELEVATION.** 46 (§78d): **NON-UNIFORM SCALE x ROTATION = SHEAR.** 47 (§79): **A FOREIGN MOD'S CACHED CURSOR CELL IS AN ASSUMPTION ABOUT COORDINATE SPACE.** 48 (§81a): **A WRITE THAT IS READ BACK BY ITS OWN CALLER IS NOT A WRITE.** 49 (§0c): **A TEST THAT PROVES FEATURE A SAYS NOTHING ABOUT FEATURE B.** 50 (§82a): **TWO OF OUR OWN PATCHES ON ONE VANILLA METHOD CANCEL SILENTLY.** GREP OUR OWN `[HarmonyPatch]` LIST FOR THE TARGET METHOD FIRST. 51 (§82b): **A FACTORY HAS USUALLY CONSUMED ITS INPUT BY THE TIME THE POSTFIX RUNS.** 52 (§83a): **AN OVERLAY MUST ASK THE SAME QUESTION THE CLICK WILL ASK, AND IT MUST NOT BE A QUESTION THAT WRITES.** 53 (§83c): **A PREDICATE PASSED IN IS CLOSED OVER THE ARGUMENTS THE CALLER ALREADY HAS.** 54 (§84a): **A CLEAN GREP IS NOT AN ABSENCE - SEARCH FOR THE CAPABILITY, NOT THE TYPE NAME.** 55 (§84.3): **"AFTER THE DUTY HAD ITS TURN" INCLUDES A FALLBACK JOB YOU WOULD NEVER CALL A REAL ONE.** 56 (§84.5): **WHEN YOU RANK CANDIDATES BY ONE COST AND FILTER THEM BY ANOTHER, THE RANKING FINDS THE FILTER'S BLIND SPOT.** 57 (§85a): **WHEN TWO SUBSYSTEMS EACH ANSWER "WHICH SIDE OF THIS THING", ONE OF THEM IS ABOUT TO BE WRONG.** 58 (§85b): **A PROPERTY OF THE ART CANNOT BE DERIVED FROM THE DEF.** 59 (§85.8): **`size` MUST BE MEASURED FROM THE DRAWING, NOT COPIED FROM `drawSize`.** 60 (§85.9): **MEASURE THE PIXELS; AND A DRAW OFFSET AND AN ART-OFFSET TABLE ARE THE SAME NUMBER TWICE.** 61 (§85c): **A COLOURED VERSION OF A GRAPHIC IS A DIFFERENT OBJECT, AND VANILLA HARD-CODES ITS TYPE.** 62 (§85d): **A TABLE OF FINISHED ANSWERS ROTS; STORE ONLY WHAT NOTHING ELSE OWNS AND DERIVE THE REST.** 63 (§85.14): **MEASURE A PATIENCE FROM THE EVENT IT NAMES.** 64 (§85.16): **A DIAGNOSTIC THAT IS OFF BY DEFAULT IS A DIAGNOSTIC THAT DOES NOT EXIST.** 65 (§85.17): **WHEN A DERIVED RULE IS RIGHT THREE TIMES OUT OF FOUR, THE FOURTH IS NOT A DIFFERENT RULE - IT IS A DEFECTIVE INPUT.** 66 (§85.19): **A DESTINATION CELL DOES NOT CONSTRAIN THE SIDE IT IS ENTERED FROM.** 67 (§85.20): **AN EARLY RETURN THAT PRESERVES STATE MUST ASK WHO SENT THE NEW ORDER.** 68 (§85.22): **WHEN THE SAME 'EXCEPTION' IS REPORTED TWICE ON ONE DEF, IT IS THE DEF'S RULE, NOT TWO EXCEPTIONS.** 69 (§86a): **WHEN YOU SUSPEND A FOREIGN MOD'S DRIVER, YOU INHERIT EVERY REQUEST THAT DRIVER SERVED.** A UI control can be nothing but a cleared field whose only consumer is the loop you switched off - so the button still draws, still responds, still clears the field, and does nothing. Enumerate what READS the state you neutralised, not just what writes it. 70 (§87a): **AN OPT-IN CORRECTION APPLIED AT N CONSUMERS IS A DEFAULT APPLIED AT THE WRONG LAYER.** If every consumer of a value wants it corrected, correct it at the source and enumerate the EXCEPTIONS instead - the exception list is finite, auditable and self-reporting, whereas the consumer list grows silently every time anyone adds a feature or installs a mod.

# 86. PERSPECTIVE SHIFT "RETURN TO CHARACTER" — **BUILT WINDOW 13, UNTESTED**

`Source/Compat/PerspectiveShiftCompat.cs` only.

**⚠⚠ 86a THE BUTTON IS NOTHING BUT A CLEARED FIELD (rule 69).** Field report: avatar on the lower floor, double-click an upper-floor colonist on the colonist bar, press "Return to character" - nothing happens. PS's `Avatar_UI.DrawCameraLockReturnButton` draws only while `State.CameraLockPosition.HasValue`, and its entire click handler is `State.CameraLockPosition = null`. It works in vanilla PS because `Avatar.UpdateCamera` then re-centres next frame. **§76 prefixes `UpdateCamera` out for the whole time the viewed band is not the avatar's** (rule 24 - remove the other driver rather than out-write it), so the press cleared the field, the button vanished, and the camera never moved.

**86.2 THE FIX: WATCH THE FALLING EDGE, AND DO NOT KEY IT ON `lockedByUs`.** `lockSeen` records the field's state each `SyncPeek`; a `true -> false` transition while `suspendCamera` is armed means "put me back on the avatar". ⚠ **In the reported repro the lock was set by PS ITSELF** - its `JumpToCurrentMapLoc` postfix fires on the colonist-bar jump - so `lockedByUs` is FALSE and a "did we set this" test misses exactly the case that was reported. Every other PS path that nulls the field (a jump whose target IS the avatar's cell, `SetAvatar`, `ClearAvatar`, load) means the same thing, and the same response is correct for all of them.

**86.3 ORDER MATTERS: BAND FIRST, RELEASE SECOND.** `ReturnToAvatar` calls `ABBandView.SetBand(avatar's band, preserveXZ:false)` and only releases the suspend once it SUCCEEDED. Releasing first would let PS drag the camera toward a band our clip refuses to draw - the window-7 curtain bug the suspend exists to prevent. An undug band makes `SetBand` refuse (with its own message) and the peek is left exactly as it was, not half-torn-down. Then `SnapToAvatar` closes the distance so PS's 10%-a-frame lerp is a no-op (same reason `FollowTransit` calls it).

**⚠ 86.4 RE-ENTRANCY IS REAL HERE:** `SetBand` calls `SyncPeek` directly (so a band change arms the peek in the same frame). `returning` guards it. `Release()` also clears `lockSeen` so a stale edge cannot survive a map change or a load.

# 87. GLOBAL CLICK-THROUGH — THE MODEL IS NOW OPT-OUT — **BUILT WINDOW 13, UNTESTED**

`Source/V2/ABMouseDescend.cs` (new), edits to `ABCombatTargeting.cs` and `ABBelowClickThrough.cs`.

**⚠⚠ 87a THE INVERSION (rule 70).** User: "make all air tiles click-through by default to save on patches. Dev targeting, psycast targeting, jumping, combat, mortars all intuitively click through air tiles as they are not selectable anyhow." Since window 7 the descend was OPT-IN, added by hand at four consumers. Every NEW consumer - a dev tool, another mod's targeter - started out broken and had to be noticed, diagnosed and patched. **The justification for inverting is that there is no reading of "I clicked the empty sky" that means the sky:** open air is Impassable, unselectable, unbuildable and undesignatable, so the raw answer is never the useful one.

**87.2 THE CHOKEPOINT IS TWO METHODS.** `UI.MouseCell` and `UI.MouseMapPosition` are both one-line wrappers over `UI.UIToMapPosition`. **⚠ THAT THIRD METHOD IS NOT PATCHED AND MUST NOT BE** - it is a pure screen-to-map transform also used for drag-box corners, the camera's own centre and map-to-UI round trips, none of which are "where is the cursor pointing". Both wrappers are needed, not one: vanilla resolves THINGS from a Vector3 clickPos but the bare CELL from `UI.MouseCell()`, and patching one without the other is precisely §82a.

**87.3 TWO FIELD-VERIFIED PATCHES DELETED AND TOMBSTONED.** `Patch_GenUI_ABThingsUnderMouseSeeThrough` and `Patch_GenUI_ABTargetsAtSeeThrough` (both §82, run #375) are redundant: vanilla now finds below-level things natively because the clickPos it searches around has already descended, and `TargetsAt` yields an already-descended `UI.MouseCell()`. **⚠ DO NOT REINSTATE EITHER** - keeping them alongside the global descend is §82a a third time (`TryResolveClicked` asks "is this open air?" about a cell already resolved to solid floor, answers no, goes silently inert, and reads to the next debugger like the rule is firing when it is not).

**⚠⚠ 87.4 POINTING IS NOT ORDERING, AND KEEPING THEM APART IS WHAT MAKES THIS SAFE.** "Which cell is under the cursor" is now global. "Where should these pawns go" also depends on the pawns and stays in `ABBelowClickThrough.TryTranslateForOrder` - field-verified (§33b/§33f) and built entirely on a RAW cursor. Rather than rewrite it against a new input contract, **`Selector.HandleMapClicks` is SUPPRESSED**, so it receives exactly the value it always has. Same for left-click selection, whose curtain clamp compares the cursor against the VIEWED band's rows and **would reject every open-air click outright** if handed a descended cell.

**87.5 THE EXCLUSION LIST, WITH THE THREE REASONS.** One `[HarmonyPatch]` with `TargetMethods` + a Finalizer, so the whole policy is auditable in one place.
- **(a) DESIGNATION AND PLACEMENT** - the user's explicit call: build and mine stay clamped (rule 1). `DesignatorManager.ProcessInputEvents/DesignatorManagerUpdate/DesignationManagerOnGUI`, `DesignationDragger.StartDrag/GetCurrentBoundary`, `Designator_Place.SelectedUpdate/DrawMouseAttachments/HandleRotation`. ⚠ The dragger is the sharp one: **a drag rect with one corner each side of a band seam designates straight across the gutter** - §46's field report (mining ghost walls a level down) in a new door.
- **(b) A DELTA OF TWO MOUSE READS** - `CameraDriver.RootSize` setter. Zoom-to-mouse is `vector = MouseMapPosition(); <zoom>; rootPos += vector - MouseMapPosition()`, and the second read is taken AFTER the camera moved. If one read sits over open air and the other over floor, the delta gains a spurious Slot and **the camera jumps a level on a scroll notch** (rule 24).
- **(c) OURS ALREADY** - `Selector.HandleMapClicks` (also protects `dragBox.start`, which `DragBox.ScreenRect` projects back to screen: a descended start anchors the selection rectangle a Slot from the press), `Selector.SelectUnderMouse`, `Selector.SelectAllMatchingObjectUnderMouseOnScreen`, `MultiPawnGotoController.ProcessInputEvents` (preserves §33f; letting `end` descend is probably an improvement, deliberately untried - ledger 14).

**⚠ 87.5b THE LIST INCRIMINATES ITSELF (rule 33).** `TargetMethods` NAMES every entry it could not resolve and errors if it resolved NONE. A silently dropped null is one exclusion quietly removed, and losing the CameraDriver entry alone presents as a camera bug with nothing in the log tying it to a rename.

**⚠ 87.5c EXPLICIT RAW BEATS AMBIENT SUPPRESSION.** `Patch_Selector_ABSelectThrough` calls `ABMouseDescend.RawMouseMapPosition()` rather than trusting that it runs inside a suppressed region - because that trust depends on a call graph nobody re-checks, and `Selector.SelectUnderMouse` has a third caller OUTSIDE `HandleMapClicks`.

**87.5d MECHANICS.** Memoised on `(frameCount, RAW cell)` - not frameCount alone, because OnGUI runs once per GUI EVENT and a MouseDown carries its own mouse position. The suppression counter is frame-stamped so a leaked push (an exception past the Finalizer, a foreign prefix skipping a patched method) costs one frame instead of wedging pointing for the session. Gated on `ABGuard.Rendering` + `ABBelowClickThrough.Enabled` (so the existing bisect action covers it) + `ABMouseDescend.Enabled`. `ABCombatTargeting.CounterReport` now reports the global descend; the old seeThroughThings/seeThroughCells pair would have read a permanent zero.

**87.6 HOW TO TEST IT.** Banded run, sky-band rig. (1) Dev tools: `AB2:` map tools and vanilla Spawning tools must place on the level SEEN through air. (2) Psycast/jump/mortar force-target through a hole - §82's #375 checks, re-run. (3) **Build a wall while hovering over open air: the ghost must stay on the VIEWED level and the placement must refuse** (rule 1). (4) **Drag-mine across a band seam: the rect must not cross the gutter.** (5) **Scroll-zoom with the cursor over open air: the camera must not jump a level.** (6) Drag-select over open air: the rectangle must start where the button went down. (7) Right-click orders both same-level and cross-level (§33b/§33f unchanged - prove it). (8) Left-click select a pawn through a hole. (9) PS + Toggleable Overlays (ledger 10).

**87.7 RESIDUE.** Our own three probe call sites (`CelestialLightingCompat` x2, `ABBandWeather`) now read the DESCENDED cell; harmless for readouts, but CelestialLighting's probe will print "IDENTITY" where it used to print "SEE-THROUGH". Double-click select-all is inside the suppressed `HandleMapClicks` and so does not see through - it did not before either.

# 88. COMBAT EXTENDED — MANNED WEAPONS ("STATIONARY MACHINE GUNS") — **OPEN, NOT STARTED**

User picked the MANNED case specifically (a pawn operating a stationary gun), not CE turrets in general.

**88.1 WHAT ALREADY WORKS.** The four §44 seams key on `Verb_LaunchProjectileCE`, `ShiftVecReport`, `ShiftTarget` and `ProjectileCE.Launch`, all of which a manned CE gun uses - so shot legality, aim space, projectile origin and the high-ground suppression model are already band-aware for it.

**⚠⚠ 88a WHAT DOES NOT, FROM DECOMPILING `CombatExtended.Building_TurretGunCE`.** It derives from `Building_Turret`, NOT `Building_TurretGun`, so `Patch_BuildingTurretGun_ABBandLocalForcedTarget` never runs on it. And `CanSetForcedTarget => mannableComp != null && PlayerControlled` - **in CE, force-targeting exists ONLY on MANNABLE turrets**, so the forced-target path IS the manned-gun path. Its `OrderAttack` does the raw `(targ.Cell - Position).LengthHorizontal` against `minRange` and `range` twice: §1's slicing rule, wrong in both directions across bands (too permissive under a mortar's min range, too restrictive past two Slots).

**88.2 THE PLAN.**
- **PART 1 (essential): `Building_TurretGunCE.OrderAttack`.** House pattern (d): a reflection-only, `Prepare()`-shape-validated prefix that handles ONLY the cross-band case by re-running the two limits band-locally via `ABCombatV2.TrySolve` and then replicating CE's short tail (`forcedTarget = targ`, `TryStartShootSomething(false)`, the holdFire message). Same-band orders fall through to CE untouched. ⚠ Considered and rejected: a transpiler (fragile to write blind) and translating `targ` for the duration (CE sets `currentTargetInt` inside the body, so the turret would fire at the translated cell for a tick).
- **PART 2: `CompFireArc.WithinFireArc`** - both `OrderAttack` and `IsValidTarget` gate on it, and the angle is raw geometry. Only defs that carry the comp.
- **PART 3: acquisition - VERIFY, DON'T ASSUME (rule 54).** `TargSearcher()` returns the MANNING PAWN when manned, and a non-`NonSnap` turret then goes through vanilla `AttackTargetFinder.BestShootTargetFromCurrentPosition`, which our §42 postfix on `BestAttackTarget` already covers. Believed fine; unproven. ⚠ A def carrying `NonSnapTurretExtension` uses CE's own `NonSnapAttackTargetFinder` instead and is NOT covered.
- **PART 4: `DrawRangeRings`** - `GenDraw.DrawRadiusRing(Position, range)`, i.e. §83.7's "turret ring viewed from another band" gap, now with an owner.
